parts.original_hypothesis: P(income<=50K) = sigmoid(-1.468 + linear_backbone + capital_gain_hinge + capgain_marital_gate + age_youth_gate + widowed_offset + nicaragua_ownchild + selfemp_guatemala_gate + armed_forces_offset + tenth_grade_offset + italy_offset + japan_offset): purely additive in the logit (output node 0 sees only the 11 child exits; weights 1 for identity exits, 0.218/-1.398/0.083/-0.027 for the four single-unit leaves). The 44 unconnected inputs (incl. fnlwgt, race:3, most countries) are zero-effect entries. Structure: a sparse linear model (marital status, education-num, relationship, sex, hours, capital-loss) plus a capital-gain effect split between a convex hinge and a gate that cancels a +4.25/+2.34 logit baseline offset (not never-married / never-married); a youth-or-Other-service OR gate; and single-category overrides for rare categories (Armed-Forces -80, Honduras +183, Guatemala +4.6, Nicaragua +3.1) fitted to tens of rows. Evidence (train, 39,073 rows): acc 0.8542, AUC 0.9108; mean-ablating the backbone drops AUC to 0.611, every other child to >=0.902. SHAP (200 train rows, mean |dP|): Married-civ 0.245, Never-married 0.066, education-num 0.052, age 0.050, Husband 0.045, capital-gain 0.036. Function preservation error 7e-16.

reference_patient.definition: the typical patient: the median training patient for every number and the most common training category for every category (not a real patient)

confidence_rules.clearly: a meaningful change in predicted risk for a typical patient (at least 5% points), the test split agrees (same sign, and its bootstrap interval over test patients excludes no benefit), and every group has at least 20 training patients
confidence_rules.consistently across patients: the claim holds for at least 90% of training patients (range across patients); this is not a significance statement
confidence_rules.on the training data only: the test split disagrees (opposite sign, or no benefit on test patients) or is unclear (its interval includes no benefit), or no test check is available
confidence_rules.slightly: the change in predicted risk for a typical patient is below 5% points
confidence_rules.the model has little data on this: a compared group has fewer than 20 training patients

settings.effect_scale: log-odds (output pre-activation) for verification; predicted risk for the typical patient for wording
